items.title: supernova: EXCBADACCESS crash on first FFT/PV/ML UGen (world.ft never set)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
<!-- For information about contributing see: https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/wiki/Contributing-directory -->
<!-- Please check there isn't already an issue on this topic. -->

Hello,

This message was written with the help of AI to solve an issue, when crashing the server with supernova. 
I do not know if it the best way to solve it.
But with this fix, there is no longer supernova crash.

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: Latest Dev
* Operating system: MacOS 27
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.): Qt 6.8 & 6.11.2

## Steps to reproduce

```supercollider
Server.supernova; // switch to the supernova executable
s.reboot;
s.waitForBoot({
    {IFFT(FFT(LocalBuf(2048), SinOsc.ar(440)))}.play;
});
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

**Expected:** the synth plays normally, like it does under scsynth.

**Actual:** supernova crashes with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` the moment the FFT
UGen is constructed.

## Problem

**File:** `server/supernova/sc/sc_plugin_interface.cpp`,
`sc_plugin_interface::initialize()`

scsynth's `World_New()` points `world->ft` at its `InterfaceTable`
(`SC_World.cpp`: `world->ft = &gInterfaceTable;`). supernova's
equivalent, `sc_plugin_interface::initialize()`, fills in its own
`sc_interface` but never assigns it to `world.ft`.

Regular UGen plugins aren't affected — they use their own file-local
`ft`, set via `load(InterfaceTable*)` at load time. But generic engine
code that only has a `World*` — `SCWorld_Allocator` in
`SC_InterfaceTable.h`, used by `scfft_create`/`scfft_destroy` for
`FFT_UGens`/`PV_ThirdParty`/`ML_UGens` — dereferences `world->ft`
directly. Since `sc_factory` is allocated via `new sc_ugen_factory`
(default-init, not value-init), that `World` struct member is never
zeroed, so this reliably crashes with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` (dereferencing a
garbage pointer) the first time any FFT-based UGen is constructed —
lazily, via `sc_synth::prepare()`, on the audio thread.

## Possible Fix

**File to modify:** `server/supernova/sc/sc_plugin_interface.cpp`
**Function:** `sc_plugin_interface::initialize()`
**Change:** one line, right after `sc_interface` is fully populated and
before `world` is otherwise initialized.

```diff
     sc_interface.fDoAsynchronousCommandEx = &do_asynchronous_command_ex;
     sc_interface.fDoAsyncUnitCommand = &do_async_unit_command;
 
+    world.ft = &sc_interface;
+
     /* initialize world */
     /* control busses */
     world.mControlBus = control_busses;
```

items.title: Scsynth doesn't clean up TCP connections

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.11.2
* Operating system: macOS 10.14
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.):

## Steps to reproduce

```supercollider
// tcp (dis)connection test - can performed locally
// start the server
~pid = (Server.program + s.options.protocol_(\tcp).maxLogins_(10).asOptionsString).unixCmd;

// then connect as if it was a remote server
(
~server = Server.remote(\localRemote, s.addr, ServerOptions().protocol_(\tcp));
~server.addr.tryConnectTCP; 
)

~server.makeGui; // check if it runs

(
// disconnect
~server.stopAliveThread;
~server.addr.tryDisconnectTCP;
~server.remove;
)

// so far, so good

// try connecting again
(
~server = Server.remote(\localRemote, s.addr, ServerOptions().protocol_(\tcp));
~server.addr.tryConnectTCP;
)

// result (posted by the server)
/*
Bad file descriptor
Bad file descriptor
Bad file descriptor
Bad file descriptor
Bad file descriptor
Bad file descriptor
...
*/

// cleanup - stop the server
thisProcess.platform.killProcessByID(~pid);
// and disconnect
(
~server.stopAliveThread;
~server.addr.tryDisconnectTCP;
~server.remove;
)

```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

<!-- Paste error messages in entirety. Use gist if very long. -->
<!-- If SC crashed, see CONTRIBUTING.md for how to make a crash report. -->

Scsynth doesn't seem to properly close/clean up after TCP connections. After disconnecting from the server using TCP connection, subsequent attempts to connect fail and the server prints `Bad file descriptor` multiple times. I looked through the existing issues and it seems like #932 might be related.
For local servers this is not an issue, since we typically quit the server when we're done with it, but for remote servers it's a perfectly valid scenario - wanting to disconnect from it, but not actually quit it.
Supernova does not have this issue.

items.title: Error when calling 'make uninstall'

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

labels.name: comp: build
labels.description: CMake build system

items.body:
I'm currently switching branches as I have an open pull request for 3.14 but normally I'm using 3.13.1. So, usually, after switching to another branch, I'm recompiling SuperCollider and then call
```
sudo make uninstall && sudo make install
```
However, there appears to be a problem with `cmake_uninstall.cmake` in 3.14:
```
CMake Error at cmake_uninstall.cmake:14 (message):
  Syntax error in cmake code at

    /home/stefan/Sources/SuperCollider/build/cmake_uninstall.cmake:14

  when parsing string

    Uninstalling \"${ENV{DESTDIR}}${file}\"

  Invalid character ('{') in a variable name: 'ENV'
```
I've been able to fix this by  adding the following block right before the `foreach` loop in `cmake_modules/cmake_uninstall.cmake.in`:
```cmake
if(DEFINED "${ENV}")
  set(ENV_DESTDIR "${ENV{DESTDIR}}")
else()
  set(ENV_DESTDIR "")
endif()
```
... and replacing every subsequent occurrence of `${ENV{DESTDIR}}` with `${ENV_DESTDIR}`.

I don't know if that's a proper fix (`ENV` doesn't seem to be defined on my machine, so I can't say what happens if it is) but if it is I could open a pull request for it.

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.14-develop
* Operating system: Arch Linux
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.): CMake 4

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
sudo make uninstall
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

Should uninstall all files of the old SuperCollider installation. Instead I get the error message posted above.

items.title: Failure to boot to specified sample rate when num input SR != num output SR

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body: ## Environment * SuperCollider version: 3.10.2 * Operating system: macOS 10.14.5 * Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.): Internal Microphone/Speakers ## Steps to reproduce Note the available I/O sample rates on my audio hardware. There are mismatches in both the available sample rates and the number of variations (but both make 96K available): Now try to boot to 96k: ```supercollider ( o = s.options; // request 96k o.sampleRate_(96000); // NOTE: MBPro only allows 96k output from built-in SPEAKERS not headphones. booo s.boot; s.waitForBoot({ "booted".postln; }) ) ``` Result: ``` Number of Devices: 3 0 : "DisplayPort" 1 : "Built-in Microph" 2 : "Built-in Output" Requested sample rate 96000.000000 was not available - attempting to use sample rate of 88200.000000 set kAudioDevicePropertyNominalSampleRate error tad! could not initialize audio. Server 'localhost' exited with exit code 0. ``` ## Expected vs. actual behavior ### Expected Boot to 96k! ### Result Fails to boot. Furthermore, tries to boot to 88.2k. ### The problem This happens here: https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/f65a1ef7bfb100f4ccb7dcab3a6dff6826be4344/server/scsynth/SC_CoreAudio.cpp#L792-L814 There are 2 details to note here: 1. There seems to be an assumption that both hardware input and output will have the same sample rates available, which you can see from above isn't always true. - The reason I think this assumption was made is because of the use of `set_union` https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/f65a1ef7bfb100f4ccb7dcab3a6dff6826be4344/server/scsynth/SC_CoreAudio.cpp#L796 - The [docs](http://www.cplusplus.com/reference/algorithm/set_union/) show: "The union of two sets is formed by the elements that are **present in either** one of the sets, or in both." [emphasis mine]. The available sample rates should be only those that *present in both* of the input and output devices. 2. The problem of not finding the the output rate of 96k, might be coming from initializing the vector `availableSampleRatesInputOutput` to a size of the _minimum_ of the available sample rates for input and output devices. https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/f65a1ef7bfb100f4ccb7dcab3a6dff6826be4344/server/scsynth/SC_CoreAudio.cpp#L795 - `set_union` subsequently starts accumulating unique sample rates but only gets to a count of 3 (the number of hardware output sample rates on my machine), which is populated by the input rates [44.1, 48, 88.2] and there's no room left for 96k. (Hence the server trying to boot to the "closest match" of 88.2, above). - Anyway that's a moot point if indeed the available rates should be _shared_ between the I/O devices (which means initializing `availableSampleRatesInputOutput` to a size of `min()` is correct). Which brings us to the Fix... ### A possible Fix Replace `set_union` with `set_intersection`. This forms a list of common sample rates between the input and output. I tested this and it solves my current problem. With this fix, when I request a Fs = 88200, because this rate isn't available to my output device, _it boots to 96k_. I'm not really in favor of this behavior. I'm of the opinion that if a sample rate is explicitly requested and that rate change fails, it's reasonable to error out, not try to boot to another sample rate. This would be a quiet failure that may cause problems depending on your use case. There may be other opinions about this and it may have already been discussed. It would be good to have feedback on whether this fix covers outlying cases. I didn't do a lot of introspecting into `AudioValueRange` and what's reported by the hardware, so there could be more to the story. I'm sure some of you have seen the guts of hardware sample rate issues and may catch an alternative issue. If this fix looks reasonable I can submit a PR after the reformat is finished.

items.title: macOS: building without specifying deployment target creates broken app bundle

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

labels.name: comp: build
labels.description: CMake build system

items.body: ## Environment * SuperCollider version: 3.15-dev * Operating system: macOS 14.7 (AArch64) * Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.): Qt 6.9.1, Xcode 16.1 ## Steps to reproduce ```sh cmake -G Xcode -D SUPERNOVA=ON .. cmake --build . --config RelWithDebInfo --target install ``` ## Expected vs. actual behavior Expected: **when building locally**, the resulting application can be opened by double-clicking. Actual behavior: the application bundle indicates that the app can't be run on this version of the OS: When trying to open it, I get: Notes: - Running SuperCollider or sclang directly from terminal still works - configuring with an explicit deployment target like `cmake -G Xcode -D SUPERNOVA=ON -D CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET="11.0" ..` and then building also works - (I tried with the deployment target "14.7", which should match my OS, and that seems to work too) Did anybody else on macOS observe this behavior? I have seen this for a while now, but this didn't use to be the case some time in the past, I don't think.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
<!-- For information about contributing see: https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/wiki/Contributing-directory -->
<!-- Please check there isn't already an issue on this topic. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.14dev [823a936]
* Operating system: Windows 11
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.):

## Steps to reproduce

```
s.boot
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

### Expected
On the first boot after launching the downloaded SuperCollider (SC), Windows OS should prompt for permission to allow `scsynth` to receive inbound data.  

### Actual
1. `scsynth` hangs, and Windows Defender occasionally displays repeated pop-ups. 
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e69c950d-b7f4-4583-a6aa-a4317cdf74a4)

2. Subsequently, the SC post window shows the following message:  
>On some Windows-based machines, Windows Defender sometimes delays server boot by one minute.
You can add scsynth.exe and/or supernova.exe *processes* to Windows Defender exclusion list to avoid this delay. It's safe.

I attempted to add it manually, but it did not function properly. The boot process for `scsynth` takes approximately three to ten minutes.  

There are three issues here:  
1. For beginners, it would be preferable to change **`Windows Defender exclusion list`** to **`Windows Defender Firewall exclusion list`**, as typing **`Windows Defender`** into the Start menu after pressing the Windows icon (⊞) opens **Windows Defender**, which does not provide access to the Windows Defender Firewall settings.  
To reach these settings, users must navigate via the **Control Panel**. Therefore, using **`Windows Defender Firewall`** or simply **`Firewall`** would make it easier for users to find the correct settings.  
2. The instructions do not specify how to add `scsynth` and `supernova` to the Windows Defender exclusion list. Each must be added twice: once for TCP and once for UDP. Furthermore, each rule must be configured for both private and public networks. How is a novice expected to be aware of this?  
3. Even after adding `scsynth` twice, the same phenomenon occurs, necessitating multiple compilation and booting attempts.  

Previously, Windows prompted users to allow `sclang`, `scsynth`, and `supernova` to receive inbound connections upon their first launch following installation.  Users simply needed to select the relevant network types, after which two rules were automatically created. Why is this feature no longer available?  Now, this happens only for `sclang`: 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/469a9b17-b727-42c7-90b4-c887a621906b)

items.title: osc bytes padding inconsistency scsynth vs supernova

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
I'm reporting a tiny inconsistency with the way osc scores are handled between scsynth and supernova. Scsynth is more permissive and supernova fails on this tiny detail. This is not an urgent issue for me since I was able to change my osc score production to account for it, but I thought I should report it anyway. 


The function .asRawOSC is adding extra bytes to d_recv synthdefs, such that
the output len is always len mod 4 = 3.

For example, compare the output of 
```
SynthDef(\NRTsineBYTES, { |out, freq = 440|
            Out.ar(out, SinOsc.ar(freq, 0, 0.2))
        }).asBytes

```
and 

```
[0.0, ['/d_recv',
        SynthDef(\NRTsineBYTES, { |out, freq = 440|
            Out.ar(out, SinOsc.ar(freq, 0, 0.2))
        }).asBytes
	]].asRawOSC
```

The result is 36 bytes at the beginning (as it should be), plus two arbitrary bytes at the end. Now simply change the name of the synthdef so that it has a different number of bytes, to get a different number of arbitrary padding bytes.

Scsynth does not seem to care about them either way, while supernova dumps core without explanation if these bytes are missing. I noticed this because I use my own osc writer that was modeled on supercollider's osc writer ~4 years ago, and my generated osc continues to work with scsynth but was not working with supernova. So I suspect that supercollider didn't add these extra bytes a few years ago and older supercollider osc scores may also not work with supernova (just a hypothesis).

items.title: Supernova seems only compatible with VS 2017 on Windows

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: both 3.12.2 and local build of 3.13.0-dev
* Operating system: Windows 10
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.): Qt 5.15.2, ASIO

## Steps to reproduce

```supercollider
Server.supernova;
s.boot;
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

I get the infamous exit code -1073741676, which is [apparently a divide-by-zero error](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47422982/c-status-1073741676).

I have seen some other people facing this issue too, like [here](https://www.reddit.com/r/supercollider/comments/wnylee/im_trying_to_boot_supernova_now_with_312/) and [here](https://scsynth.org/t/win11-supernova/6377).

I compiled SC from source (with Supernova), and it seems that strangely enough if I am building in Debug mode, Supernova manages to boot with some quirks:
- a) I get the [thread affinity warnings](https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/issues/5540) that indeed go away if I build from [this PR](https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/pull/5618).
- b) when I try to use the default Synth, I get an error: `OffsetOut_Ctor: alloc failed, increase server's RT memory (e.g. via ServerOptions)` which does not seem affected by the size of `Server.default.options.memSize`. However if I define a SynthDef, that seems to work okay.

SC 3.13.0-dev in Debug mode (this works):
```supercollider
Server.supernova;
s.boot;

(
SynthDef("sine", { arg freq=800, chan=0;
    var osc;
    osc = SinOsc.ar(freq, 0, mul:1/600);
    Out.ar(chan, osc);
}).writeDefFile;
)

(
var group = ParGroup.new();
600.do{ Synth(\sine, target: group) };
)
```

BUT if I try this (still in SC 3.13.0-dev in Debug):
```supercollider
Server.supernova;
s.boot;

(
var group = ParGroup.new();
n = 10
n.do{ Synth(\default, target: group) };
)
```
I get a `OffsetOut_Ctor: alloc failed, increase server's RT memory (e.g. via ServerOptions)` n times.

If I build in Release mode, Supernova refuses to boot with the familiar exit code -1073741676, again.
SC 3.12.2 (public release) OR 3.13.0-dev built in Release mode:
```supercollider
Server.supernova;
s.boot;
```

I get:
```
Booting server 'localhost' on address 127.0.0.1:57110.
Supernova booting
Server 'localhost' exited with exit code -1073741676.
```

So there is something with building in Release mode that produces a divide-by-zero error when Supernova tries to boot. It seems to work (minus the default synth alloc error) if I build in Debug mode.

items.title: Scheduling problems on Apple M1

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.12.2, 3.13.0-rc-1 arm64 and x64
* Operating system: macOS Monterey 12.6.1 and Ventura

## Steps to reproduce

```supercollider
SynthDef(\imp, { OffsetOut.ar(0, Impulse.ar(0)); FreeSelf.kr(Impulse.kr(0)); }).add;

(
t = Task({
	10000.do({ arg i;
		Synth(\imp);
		0.05.wait;
		});
	});
)

t.start;
t.stop;
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

I have done different tests sending messages from scland and from another OSC client (Antescofo) to scsynth and I find scheduling problems (rhythmic irregularity or interruptions). 
If I launch the Task process (example above Steps to reproduce) on a Mac M1 the rhythm generated by scland in scsynth has irregularities and is not completely stable. For example if MacOS starts to make an indexation (Spotligth), if I connect to the internet or switch from one application to another (command+tab), there are interruptions. It seems that every time the system does a background operation, there are interruptions sending or receiving OSC messages.
I have done several tests on 2 MacBook Pro M1 with Monterey (12.6.1) and a MacBook Air M1 with Ventura.
This problem does not happen on a MacBook Pro with Intel processor running SC 3.12.2.
I've tried with the x64 version on Rosetta and native ARM64 and the problem is the same...

Apparently there is a priority problem, but using the 'renice' command in the terminal and increasing the priority of scsynth and sclang process there seems to be a very small improvement, but it doesn't solve the problem.

Any idea how to solve this problem? To make it work like on an Intel processor without interruptions ?

Thanks,

José

items.title: Memory leak: UGen Ctors get called over and over again when they throw exceptions (e.g. alloc failed)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.12
* Operating system: Linux
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.): Jack

## Steps to reproduce
I encounter this using PartConv, but I suspect it's something more general.
```supercollider
// allocate a big IR buffer
b = Buffer.alloc(s, PartConv.calcBufSize(2048, (numFrames: 44100 * 300)).asInteger);
// this is too much for my 8GB ram, trying to play PartConv causes alloc failed
x = { PartConv.ar(Silent.ar, 2048, b) }.play;
// if x runs for a little while, it eventually prints "server disconnected shared memory interface"
x.free;
// then if I try to allocate anything else, I still get "alloc failed"
{DelayN.ar(Silent.ar, 1)}.play
```

on supernova:

```supercollider
{DelayN.ar(Silent.ar, 100)}.play
// -> Failed to allocate memory for   ugen.
// Server 'localhost' exited with exit code 0.
// server 'localhost' disconnected shared memory interface
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior
I would expect `x.free` to cleanup as if the "too big" memory allocation never happened, so that I can still allocate a smaller amount of memory.
What I observe is that on failed allocation, the UGen constructor runs repeteadly (once for every time the alloc failed error is printed), and the destructor never runs (I observed this by adding a few Print statements in UGens constructors and destructors). Destructors are not called even when the synth or the whole Node Tree is freed.
This is by the way how error messages are "flooding" (relating to #3563): the error occurs again and again at every processing block.

I observed this looping behavior also with DelayN, but I can't get to the "disconnected shared memory interface" point with DelayN.

On supernova the server crashes when I try to allocate too much memory.... I assume it might be linked but it looks also like a different issue to me.

items.title: Codesigning issues on macOS with M1 (ARM64) processors

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

labels.name: comp: build
labels.description: CMake build system

items.body:
<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: `develop` branch
* Operating system: macOS 11.6
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.): M1 MacBookPro, XCode 13.0

## TL;DR

Apple requires _all_ binaries to be signed in order to run on Apple ARM64 processors (M1 family), including the binaries built locally. XCode does sign all the binaries when building from their IDE. We currently [disable codesigning in CMake](https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/pull/5362) due to issues with signing dependencies.

## Steps to build SuperCollider on M1 MBP

**Note: On ARM64 Qt5 from homebrew does not provide the WebEngine, so we need to disable its use** (#5584)

- Install all the dependencies using homebrew, as indicated in the `README_MACOS.md`
- Configure and build as usual, except without QtWebEngine
```sh
cmake -G Xcode -D CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=`brew --prefix qt5` -D SUPERNOVA=ON -D SC_USE_QTWEBENGINE=OFF ..
cmake --build . --target install --config RelWithDebInfo
```
The build should finish successfully. However, the signatures of the binaries are invalid. To rectify that, we need to re-sign all the binaries
- Sign the binaries and libraries
```sh
# assuming you are in the build folder
codesign --deep --force --verify --verbose --timestamp --sign "Apple Development" Install/SuperCollider/SuperCollider.app Install/SuperCollider/SuperCollider.app/Contents/MacOS/*  Install/SuperCollider/SuperCollider.app/Contents/Resources/*  Install/SuperCollider/SuperCollider.app/Contents/Frameworks/*
```

Now you should be able to run your build.

We need to sign everything with our developer certificate (ad-hoc signing doesn't seem to be an option). If you only have a single certificate, you should be able to use "Apple Development" as the identity. Otherwise check the existing certificates using `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` and use the SHA of the chosen certificate instead of "Apple Development".

## Possible solutions

I'm guessing the proper way to "fix" this is to re-integrate codesigning into our CMake workflow, but I'm not sure how to achieve that with all the dependencies, passing the credentials etc.

Comments always welcome!

```supercollider
(

)

s.dumpOSC; // optionally see OSC messages

// ------------------
// functional example
~group = Group(); // create group
~group.set(\phase, [\c0, \c1]); // crash

// ---------------
// musical example
(
~proxy = ProxySpace(s);
~buffer = Buffer.read(s, Platform.resourceDir +/+ "sounds/a11wlk01-44_1.aiff");
~proxy[\warp] = {Warp1.ar(1, ~buffer, \phase.kr(0 ! 2)) * -12.dbamp};
~proxy[\warp].play;
~proxy[\phase] = {LFDNoise3.kr(0.3 ! 2)};
)
~proxy[\warp].set(\phase, ~proxy[\phase]); // crash
~proxy[\warp].map(\phase, ~proxy[\phase]); // also crash
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

Calling `.set` on a group with an array containing control mapping messages crashes supernova. This works fine in scsynth.

items.title: supernova binds to 0.0.0.0 by default

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.11/develop
* Operating system: macOS
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.):

## Steps to reproduce

```supercollider
Server.supernova;
s.boot;
```
in terminal
```
lsof -i UDP
```
result:
```
...
supernova 34622 marcin   19u  IPv4 0xdd06c08b2563682f      0t0  UDP *:57110
...
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

It seems that `supernova` binds its UDP or TCP socket to `0.0.0.0` by default, similarly to what `scsynth` used to do: https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/issues/4496. See this issue for more details and discussion.

Currently `scsynth` binds to `127.0.0.1`; `supernova` should probably be doing the same.

EDIT: according to #4496, a fix for `supernova` would be more involved (adding a new command line argument).

items.title: Win 10 (?, not 7): SC 64-bit (VS) & JackAudio: sc cannot coexist with JackAudio/JackRouter on Windows

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
If you've ended up with a server that doesn't boot anymore after you installed jackd (even after a jackd uninstall), or if you installed SC and found the server doesn't boot - and you have JackAudio 64-bit installed on your system:

Don't despair, don't format your harddisk! :)

You are likely running SC 3.8 64-bit (VS install)

- check if the following helps: unregister the JackRouter.dll:
    - open an administrator shell and go to the Jack app-folder, usually: C:\Program Files\Jack
    - go to the 64bits
    - execute `regsvr32 /u .\JackRouter.dll`
    - reboot your computer
    - try if the server boots
- if not, likely something didn't go cleanly in you Jackd install. In that case even uninstalling Jack is not enough
    - open the registry editor (`regedit`) and search for "JackRouter". Delete the key `regsvr32`. You'll get a couple of finds.

That should do it.

Note that SC 64-bit (SC 3.8 VS-compile) does *not* work with JackAudio on Windows. The current developer version of SC (3.9dev) can be built to a 64-bit version using MSYS2/MinGW. This flavor will work with JackAudio.

If you can afford to use JackAudio-32, you can also use the 32-bit version of SCWin 3.8, and the two will cooperate. If you are bound to 64-bit, e.g. because you are using a 64-bit DAW with JackAudio, there is no known solution at the time of this writing (SC 3.8, Feb 2017).

items.body:
<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: develop
* Operating system: macOS 10.13
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.): CMake 3.18

## Steps to reproduce

Upgrade CMake. Configure and build.


## Expected vs. actual behavior

<!-- Paste error messages in entirety. Use gist if very long. -->
<!-- If SC crashed, see CONTRIBUTING.md for how to make a crash report. -->


On macos we use Portaudio with Supernova.
During configuring, when `find_package(Portaudio REQUIRED)` is [called](https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/develop/server/supernova/CMakeLists.txt#L154), we get following output from CMake:


```
CMake Warning (dev) at /usr/local/Cellar/cmake/3.18.3/share/cmake/Modules/FindPackageHandleStandardArgs.cmake:273 (message):
  The package name passed to `find_package_handle_standard_args` (PkgConfig)
  does not match the name of the calling package (Portaudio).  This can lead
  to problems in calling code that expects `find_package` result variables
  (e.g., `_FOUND`) to follow a certain pattern.
Call Stack (most recent call first):
  /usr/local/Cellar/cmake/3.18.3/share/cmake/Modules/FindPkgConfig.cmake:59 (find_package_handle_standard_args)
  cmake_modules/FindPortaudio.cmake:22 (include)
  server/supernova/CMakeLists.txt:155 (find_package)
This warning is for project developers.  Use -Wno-dev to suppress it.

-- Found PkgConfig: /usr/local/bin/pkg-config (found version "0.29.2")
```

Inside [FindPortaudio.cmake](https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/develop/cmake_modules/FindPortaudio.cmake), the `PORTAUDIO2_LIBRARIES` variable seems initially to be set to a list: `portaudio;-framework CoreAudio;-framework AudioToolbox;-framework AudioUnit;-framework Carbon`, and then the resulting `PORTAUDIO_LIBRARIES` becomes 
```
/usr/local/Cellar/portaudio/19.6.0/lib/libportaudio;-framework CoreAudio;-framework AudioToolbox;-framework AudioUnit;-framework Carbon.dylib
```
It seems that we should only be taking the first element of that list. The correct paht should be `/usr/local/Cellar/portaudio/19.6.0/lib/libportaudio.dylib`. Unfortunately I can't easily revert CMake version to compare the behavior with the previous version.

This causes a linking error when compiling supernova:
```
clang: error: no such file or directory: '/usr/local/Cellar/portaudio/19.6.0/lib/libportaudio'
```
because the path is incorrect.

I created a workaround that sets seem to set the path correctly: https://github.com/dyfer/supercollider/commit/8e3d71beec0881a945e9336aab24085b2a8bd246 However, I'm not sure how to avoid the warning from CMake and what is the root cause of the problem.

* SuperCollider version: 3.11.0
* Operating system: Windows 10
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.):

## Steps to reproduce

```supercollider
g = Group();
Ndef(\a).parentGroup_(g).source = {SinOsc.ar(440!2) };
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

Expected the new NodeProxy's internal Group to be created inside the Group `g`. However, you get an error message instead:

```txt
NodeProxy:parentGroup_ : cannot make non-playing node parentGroup
```

According to @jamshark70, the new Group should have `isPlaying` set by default, as soon as it's "alive" on the Server, as this is the mechanism used by `NodeWatcher`. See discussion here, beginning with this message: https://scsynth.org/t/cpu-headroom-supernova-multiple-servers/2752/6

My "workaround" (which shouldn't be necessary) is the following -- manually setting `isPlaying`:

```supercollider
g = Group().isPlaying_(true);
Ndef(\a).parentGroup_(g).source = {SinOsc.ar(440!2) };
```

items.title: Supernova doesn't support remote login

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.11
* Operating system: Doesn't matter

## Steps to reproduce

In a terminal:

```
$ sclang
...
sc3> Server.supernova;
sc3> s.options.maxLogins = 2; s.boot;
```

Then in IDE:

```supercollider
Server.default = s = Server.remote(\remote, NetAddr("127.0.0.1", 57110));
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

Expected behavior should match scsynth:

```
Requested notification messages from server 'remote'
remote: server process has maxLogins 2 - adjusting my options accordingly.
remote: setting clientID to 1, as obtained from server process.
remote : setting clientID to 1.
```

Actual behavior:

```
Requested notification messages from server 'remote'
remote: no maxLogins info from server process.
remote: setting clientID to 1, as obtained from server process.
WARNING: Server remote couldn't set clientID to 1 - outside of allowed server.maxNumClients range of 0 - 0. clientID is still 0.
```

Updates to scsynth boot/handshaking logic changed the OSC spec for `/notify` done and failure replies. Supernova was never updated for the new spec.

TBH I'm a bit worried about supernova's maintenance status. It's starting to smell like an abandoned project -- nobody's intention to let this happen, but let's be honest. There are years-old bugs and nobody is stepping up to fix them. It may be time for an RFC about the future of multicore support in SC. I hesitate to open an RFC by myself because parallel real-time processing is *way* outside my expertise -- just reminding for now that the current situation is not really sustainable.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
<!--- Hi, and thanks for contributing! -->

<!--- Before opening a new issue, please search our existing issues to see if anyone else has had the-->
<!--- same issue as you. Make sure to provide a general summary of the issue in the Title above! -->

Environment
-----------

* Your SuperCollider version: 3.10dev
* Your operating system and version: macOS 10.13


Steps to reproduce (for bugs)
-----------------------------

```supercollider
//set your default devices to internal soundcard (2 inputs/outputs)
Server.supernova;
s.options.numOutputBusChannels_(4); //choose number larger than the soundcard provides
s.boot;
s.meter; //no sound from the input
//moreover, the input busses are unusable
x = {PinkNoise.ar(-48.dbamp)}.play(outbus: s.options.numOutputBusChannels); //signal accumulates

x.free;
s.quit;

```

Error message (for bugs)
------------------------

no error

Expected Behavior
-----------------

Sound input should work, even if specified number of output channels exceeds number of channels available in the hardware.

Current Behavior
----------------

No signal from audio interface appears on the input busses.
If one attempts playing a signal on an input bus from a synth, the signal weirdly accumulates and eventually distorts.

Actually, it sounds almost exactly like an impulse at control rate:
```SuperCollider
x = {Impulse.ar(ControlRate.ir) * -12.dbamp}.play;
```
You can listen to the input to check (careful, this will quickly overload/distort!)
```SuperCollider
y = {SoundIn.ar(0)}.play;
x = {PinkNoise.ar(-48.dbamp)}.play(outbus: s.options.numOutputBusChannels); //signal accumulates
s.freqscope;

x.free; y.free;
```




Note: this applies to supernova on macOS, which uses PortAudio. I also tested with scsynth compiled with PortAudio (on macOS) but was not able to reproduce the issue, so it's not a purely PortAudio issue, but supernova / PortAudio.

I have not tested on other platforms (I have a feeling it might affects supernova on Windows, but that doesn't currently build so...).

<!--- Hi, and thanks for contributing! -->

<!--- Before opening a new issue, please search our existing issues to see if anyone else has had the-->
<!--- same issue as you. Make sure to provide a general summary of the issue in the Title above! -->

Environment
-----------

* Your SuperCollider version: 3.10-beta1
* Your operating system and version: macOS 10.13.06

<!--- If you are compiling from a branch other than master, please provide the SHA1 hash of the commit -->
<!--- Include any other relevant details about your environment (Qt version, audio driver, etc.) -->

Steps to reproduce (for bugs)
-----------------------------

```supercollider
//caution - this will force close the interpreter!
(
Server.scsynth;
s.addr.port = 57130; //set non-default port
s.waitForBoot({
	"killall sclang".unixCmd; //kill sclang (no cleanup - server will keep running)
})
)
//-----
//boot the interpreter manually, then:
//-----
//check if the old server is still running - it probably is
"ps ax | grep -E '[s]csynth|[s]upernova'".systemCmd; 

(
Server.supernova; //switch servers;
Server.killAll; //tries to kill supernova; scsynth keeps running;
s.boot; //boots fine, since the old server was using a non-default port
)

//check for scsynth and supernova - both are running
"ps ax | grep -E '[s]csynth|[s]upernova'".systemCmd; 

//you can manually kill scsynth... but should Server.killAll have done it?
"killall scsynth".systemCmd;
```

Error message (for bugs)
------------------------

(No error message)

Expected Behavior
-----------------
This is maybe a very edge case...
If one ends up with a dangling server, and then switches from ```scsynth``` to ```supernova``` (or vice versa), then ```Server.killAll``` option will not necessarily kill the old process. This happens only if the dangling process was booted with a non-default port number or if it's not responding to OSC messages anymore.


Current Behavior
----------------

```Server.killAll``` attempts to kill only the currently chosen server - either ```scsynth``` or ```supernova```. However it also sends ```\quit``` OSC message, so any dangling but responsive server _should_ still quit.

I'm considering whether ```Server.killAll``` should kill both ```supernova``` and ```scsynth``` instances. What do you think?

<!--- Thanks again for contributing! -->

<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.10.3
* Operating system: macOS 10.13.6
* Other details (Qt version, audio driver, etc.):

## Steps to reproduce
This was previous reported as issue with PartConv, but actually seems to apply to FFT processing in general on my machine.

```supercollider
(
//CAREFUL! this will create LOUD DISTORTION
~numSynths = 2;

~syncBetweenSynths = true; //works fine
// ~syncBetweenSynths = false; //THIS WILL CREATE LOUD DISTORTION

Server.supernova;

s.waitForBoot {

	SynthDef(\pt_test, {arg playbuf = 0, irbuf = 0, amp = 0.5, out = 0;
		var sig, chain;
		sig = SinOsc.ar(300, 0, amp);
		chain = FFT(LocalBuf(2048), sig);
		sig = IFFT(chain); // inverse FFT
		Out.ar(out, sig * amp);
	}).add;

	~target = ParGroup();
	s.sync;

	~allSynths = ~numSynths.collect({|inc|
		var synth = Synth(\pt_test, [\amp, -26.dbamp, \out, inc], ~target);
		if(~syncBetweenSynths, {s.sync});
		synth;
	});
}
)

//free everything
(
~target.free;
currentEnvironment.clear;
)
```

## Expected vs. actual behavior

<!-- Paste error messages in entirety. Use gist if very long. -->
<!-- If SC crashed, see CONTRIBUTING.md for how to make a crash report. -->
Actual behavior:
When multiple ~~PartConvs~~ synths with FFT are started in a parallel group at the same time, they output loud distortion. If they are started after waiting for the server to allocate resources for the previous Synth, or if it's a regular group, they work fine.

Expected behavior: 
Multiple ~~PartConvs~~ synths with FFT  start simultaneously in a ParGroup without issue.

## Discussion:
It seems to be an issue with the vDSP implementation, as indicated in the [source](https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/develop/common/SC_fftlib.cpp#L24). Building supernova with the internal `Green FFT` library fixes the problem (although that's arguably not a proper "fix").

items.body:
I'm running SuperCollider 3.10.3 and I'm using Jack with supernova on macOS 10.14. Everything works perfectly, but when I start a pattern such as:
```
Pbind(\degree, Pwhite(0, 10)).play
```
sclang returns a "late: 0.620066" message. I believe this has to do with the latency calculation when supernova boots:
```
Booting server 'localhost' on address 127.0.0.1:57110.
Supernova booting
Available Audio Devices:
0: Built-in Microphone (2 inputs, 0 outputs)
1: Built-in Output (0 inputs, 2 outputs)
2: JackRouter (4 inputs, 4 outputs)

opening portaudio device name: JackRouter / JackRouter
opening portaudio device name: JackRouter / JackRouter
  latency: -394928160
opened portaudio device name: JackRouter / JackRouter
  Sample rate: 48000.000
  Latency (in/out): 81250.814 / 81250.815 sec
Supernova ready
Requested notification messages from server 'localhost'
localhost: no maxLogins info from server process.
localhost: keeping clientID (0) as confirmed by server process.
StageLimiter active
Shared memory server interface initialized
```
Changing block size and sample rate changes the latency value but it doesn't solve the problem. It seems that supernova calculates a wrong latency value when using JackRouter as the audio device.  Everything works fine, when I'm not using Jack.

UPDATE:
I found that the problem is solved by setting the ServerOption useSystemClock = true.

items.title: scsynth's network socket should bind to 127.0.0.1 by default rather than 0.0.0.0

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
<!-- Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines. -->

## Environment

* SuperCollider version: 3.10.2

## Description

supercollider is intended to be run on local machines, and security is not really a top priority for the platform. however, right now, scsynth binds its UDP or TCP socket to `0.0.0.0` by default:

https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/develop/server/scsynth/scsynth_main.cpp#L140

which means that it listens on all interfaces. usually this means that anyone in your local network can mess with scsynth, which isn't what 99% of users want. even laptop ensembles tend to have everyone run their own client/server and most of the communication happens between clients.

simply changing this to `127.0.0.1` will be a more reasonable default configuration. this will not affect most users, but will impact people doing networked clients, who will need to set `-B 0.0.0.0`. see #4497.

disclaimer: i am not really great with network programming, so any insight from someone who knows better would be greatly appreciated!

## Securing an existing supercollider installation

until this is fixed, this hack can secure scsynth by placing it in your startup file:

`Server.program = "scsynth -B 127.0.0.1";`

## What about supernova?

supernova, as far as i can tell, does not support the `-B` flag, so getting supernova up to speed with scsynth is more involved. i'm not personally interested in maintaining supernova anymore, so i can't help with such issues.

items.title: Supernova doesn't guarantee OSC message ordering

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issues that relate to unexpected/unwanted behavior. Don't use for PRs.

items.body:
Supernova has actually two NRT queues which are performed on different threads: 
1) the "system" thread for asynchronous tasks
2) the "io" thread for outgoing OSC messages.

While simply commands like /b_info send the reply on the "io" thread, asynchronous commands send the `/done` message (in stage 4) on the "system" thread, mostly because they have to finish some work (e.g. freeing memory).

In practice this can lead to various race conditions, e.g.:
* `/synced` sent *before* `/done`
* `/b_info` (from a `/b_query` completion message) sent *after* `/done`

See the following discussions:

https://www.listarc.bham.ac.uk/lists/sc-dev/msg59118.html
https://www.listarc.bham.ac.uk/lists/sc-dev/msg59108.html

---

I see three solutions:

1) Always send `/done` messages on the io thread
If this works as expected, it should be the most elegant solution as it keeps the advantage of having a dedicated io thread (so that long asynchronous commands don't block synchronous commands or node replies)

2) Only keep a single NRT thread
This means we get the same design as scsynth and don't run into any race conditions. Note that the FIFO must be multi-producer because triggers/node replies might be sent from RT helper threads.

3) Only keep the `io_interpreter` for client notifications which are sent autonomously from UGens, e.g. node replies and triggers, so they are not blocked by long asynchronous tasks.
The question is what to do with Node state messages (e.g. '/n_end'). One the one hand, they might be sent as the result of a completion message and should therefore go to the 'system_interpreter'; on the other hand, they might be sent from RT helper threads via plugin interface methods (`done_action`, `node_end`, `node_set_run`) and should therefore go to the thread-safe 'io_interpreter'.

Here's a PR which implements 1): https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/pull/4460
